Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually come with too many software restrictions. The platform can run most major computer applications, and there are plenty of useful Mac-exclusive apps to choose from.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games are currently performing better on Mac than ever before, whether through official or unofficial channels...

Apple has its own Game Porting Toolkit, which helps developers evaluate how their Windows games will run on Mac, aiming to encourage and facilitate game ports to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito points out, this toolkit has also been used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac — he himself is one of them. He noted that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, using GTA V as an example.

After testing the fourth beta version of the Game Porting Toolkit for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with the M4 Pro chip, he found that these performance improvements essentially transformed the experience of running demanding Windows games... On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using the same in-game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate increased from approximately 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to approximately 176 fps in GPTK 4 beta, an improvement of about 66%. The game runs quite smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings at 2K resolution.

He acknowledges that not every game will see such significant improvements, but he hopes these advances will encourage game developers to consider Mac as a viable platform.
